How the parts of the bot fit together, how a message flows through them, which outside services it talks to, the project's own vocabulary, and what to update when you add something.

For the full design history of each feature, see `CONTEXT.md`. For lookup tables (settings, commands, timers), see `docs/REFERENCE.md`.

## The parts

| Part | Files | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Entry point | `bot.js` | Reads `.env`, creates the clients, wires the modules, runs start-up and the cron jobs. |
| Shared state | `src/state.js` | Every Map and timer constant, one object shared by all modules. |
| Discord front end | `src/commands.js`, `src/slash-commands.js` | Message handling and answer routing; staff slash commands. |
| Telegram front end | `telegram/telegram-adapter.js` | The same routing for Telegram, plus the staff DM panel and moderation. |
| Intent and scam detection | `src/intent.js`, `src/utils.js` (spoof helpers) | Haiku intent classification, scam layers 1–3, intent logs. |
| Answering | `src/claude.js`, `src/price-fetcher.js` | Scam-concern check (layers 4–5), RAG retrieval and re-ranking, prices, the Sonnet call, conversation state. |
| Knowledge base | `src/rag.js`, `src/embedder.js`, `src/kb-sync.js`, `src/blog-scraper.js`, `src/kb-monitor.js`, `src/knowledge-loader.js` | Indexing and search, sitemap sync and scraping, health checks. |
| Moderation store | `src/scam-tracker.js`, `src/toggles.js` | Scammer infractions and feature toggles (both under `data/`). |
| Reports | `weekly-report/` | Community reports and join/leave stats. |
| Tools | `scripts/`, `intent/*.js` | One-off and diagnostic scripts — not loaded by the bot. |

This table splits the code by layer. To split it by **feature** (answering, Discord scam blocking, Telegram moderation, reports), for example to reuse one on another server, see "Feature map" below.

Most modules are **factories**: `bot.js` calls `createClaudeModule(...)`, `createIntentModule(...)`, `createMonitorModule(...)`, `registerMessageHandler(...)`, `createSlashHandler(...)` and `createTelegramAdapter(...)` once, passing in the clients, config and other modules. Modules never read the Discord client or `.env` themselves (except `state.js` for `STAFF_WAIT_MINUTES` and `embedder.js` for the Voyage key).

## How a message flows

A Discord message in an answer channel (Telegram follows the same path in `telegram-adapter.js`):

1. **`messageCreate`** (`src/commands.js`) ignores bots. Ticket and collab channels are logged and dropped.
2. The message is logged to `intent/dc-intent-log.jsonl` (general, support and the Chinese channel).
3. **Fingerprinted scam images**: a non-staff message with an image staff marked as scam → forwarded to #ai, then `takeScamAction`. Then the **name-spoof check** (Layer 3): a non-staff sender whose name resembles staff, offering private help → `takeScamAction`. Then **linked tweets**: a non-staff message with an X/Twitter link has the tweet read first (`src/tweet-check.js`, FxTwitter); a fake help-desk or known campaign tweet → `takeScamAction` at once, and a message that is only a link to an ordinary tweet is later spared by `takeScamAction`. Then the **new-member link rule**: a non-staff message with a non-X link typed without http, posted within `NEW_MEMBER_LINK_MS` of joining, goes to `detectBareLinkLLM` (Haiku, given the whole message and the sender's own previous message) → `takeScamAction` if it says they are sharing a website, otherwise on to routing.
4. The Chinese channel stops here after a scam check. Staff text commands, the explanation embed, knowledge capture (announcements, tweets) and Q&A learning are handled next.
5. **Routing** picks a scenario:
   - **0** — a reply to the bot's clarifying question → continue the conversation.
   - **0.5** — a reply to any bot answer → classify; answer only a "respond" intent.
   - **1** — an @mention → classify (scam / staff-ping), then answer.
   - **2** — an @mention as a reply to someone else → moderate the original, answer it.
   - **3** — no mention → classify; a "respond" intent waits `STAFF_WAIT_MS` for staff, then auto-answers. Messages arriving meanwhile join the same batch.
6. **`answerQuestion`** (`src/claude.js`): escalate after 2 answers in 2 hours; otherwise check for scam concern, search the KB (`searchKB`), re-rank with Haiku, add live prices if asked, call Sonnet, send the reply (split under 2,000 characters) and store the conversation for follow-ups.

Any scenario that classifies `scam-content` calls `takeScamAction` (delete, escalating timeout, alert) when the scam blocker is ON. After the message is handled, a DM request that was left up and is addressed to another member starts a 2-hour watch (`watchDmHelper`): if its sender then deletes part of that conversation, `takeScamAction` runs on it.

Knowledge flows in separately: `/sync` scrapes the docs and blog sitemaps into `knowledge-base/`, the announcement scan appends facts to curated files, new pages and facts are checked against the corrections and `core-facts.md` (proposed updates go to `corrections/_drafts/` for review), and `buildIndex()` re-embeds only changed chunks into `knowledge-base/.embeddings-cache.json`.

| Voyage AI | Embeddings for RAG | `src/embedder.js` |
| Dexscreener | Live token prices | `src/price-fetcher.js` |
| FxTwitter (public API, no key) | Reading linked X/Twitter posts for the scam blocker | `src/tweet-check.js` |
| `docs.riverai.inc`, `blog.riverai.inc` | Sitemap sync and scraping (needs WARP) | `src/kb-sync.js`, `src/blog-scraper.js` |

## Data on disk

| Path | Written by | In git? |
|---|---|---|
| `knowledge-base/` | sync, capture, `/add-correction`, `/blog`, announcement scan | yes (except the embedding cache and `corrections/_drafts/`) |
| `channel-learning/<channel>/qa-log.md` | Q&A learning | no — local only |
| `intent/*.jsonl` | intent, ticket and collab logs | no |

## Glossary

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| KB | The knowledge base: Markdown files under `knowledge-base/` (plus local `channel-learning/`). |
| RAG | Retrieval-augmented generation: find the most relevant KB chunks, send only those to Claude. |
| Chunk | A ~1,500-character piece of a KB file, embedded as one vector. |
| Correction | A hand-written file in `knowledge-base/corrections/` that overrides wrong docs or blogs; ranked 1.3× in search. |
| Core facts | `knowledge-base/core-facts.md` — injected into every system prompt. |
| Curated announcement file | `exchanges-and-token.md`, `ecosystem-milestones.md`, `important-notices.md` — indexed summaries of announcements. |
| Raw capture | `<Month>_ann/` and `<Month>_tweet/` week files written as messages arrive; never indexed. |
| `<!-- EXCLUDE -->` marker | Wraps a section of a KB file that must not be indexed (closed by `<!-- /EXCLUDE -->`). |
| Intent | One of 15 categories Haiku gives a message; see `intent/intent-taxonomy.md`. |
| Respond intents | `help-seeking`, `troubleshooting`, `onboarding`, `factual-question` — the only ones answered. |
| Scenario 0 / 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 3 | How a message reached the bot (see "How a message flows"). |
| Staff wait | The pause before a Scenario 3 auto-answer, so staff can reply first. |
| Batch | All of one user's messages that arrive during a staff wait, answered together once. |
| Staff engaged | Staff have just replied to a user, so auto-answers to that user are blocked for 3 minutes. |
| Community step-in | Another member answers a pending question; cancels the auto-answer only if it is genuine help. |
| Self-resolution | The asker says it's sorted ("ok", "fixed"); cancels their pending auto-answer. |
| ANSWER / CLARIFY / ESCALATE | The tag Claude starts each reply with: answered, asking one question, or sending to a ticket. |
| Scam layers 1–5 | 1–2 check a scammer's message (regex, then Haiku); 3 is the name-spoof detector; 4–5 check a worried user's question (regex, then Haiku) to add the safety message. |
| Scam blocker | The toggle that lets fingerprinted scam images, layers 1–3, the linked-tweet check and the new-member link rule delete the message and time the sender out. |
| Infraction | One recorded scam-blocker action against a user (`data/scammer-list.json`). |
| Watch / mute / kick / ban | Telegram moderation modes, re-applied on rejoin. |
| Staff panel | The Telegram DM menu (`/start`) for reports and member stats. |
| Explanation embed | Staff "@bot + message link": shows which sources an answer used. |
| Q&A learning | Saving a user question (one the classifier marked answerable) with the staff reply into `channel-learning/` for RAG. |
| Date floor | `BLOG_SINCE_DATE` / `effectiveSinceDate`: blog posts older than this are not synced. |
| WARP | Cloudflare's VPN client; must be on for scraping. |

## Feature map

The bot does four jobs: answering questions, scam blocking on Discord, moderation on Telegram, and reports. The code is organised by layer and platform, not by these jobs, so most files serve more than one. This section maps each job to its exact code (file, section heading, function name) so it can be lifted into a new project, or the bot reorganised later. Mapped from a full read of the code on 2026-11-15; update it when code moves between jobs.

### At a glance

| Job | Files that are only this job | Mixed into shared files | How hard to extract |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Answering | `src/claude.js`, `src/rag.js`, `src/embedder.js`, `src/blog-scraper.js`, `src/kb-monitor.js`, `src/knowledge-loader.js`, `src/price-fetcher.js`, `src/kb-sync.js` (apart from usage tracking) | Routing in `src/commands.js` and `telegram/telegram-adapter.js`; the classifier in `src/intent.js` | Medium: the files are clean, the routing has to be split out |
| 2. Discord scam blocking | `src/scam-tracker.js`, `src/tweet-check.js` | Most of it is inside `src/commands.js`; layers 1–2 in `src/intent.js`; layer 3 in `src/utils.js` and `bot.js` | **Hardest**: it has no entry point of its own (see "Coupling to undo") |
| 3. Telegram moderation | — | All of it is inside `telegram/telegram-adapter.js`, plus `checkWatchedFUD` in `src/intent.js` | Medium: self-contained, but in the same file as Telegram answering |
| 4. Reports | `weekly-report/` (all three files) | Its input logs are written by `src/commands.js`, `src/intent.js` and the Telegram adapter; its staff panel is in the adapter | **Easiest**: it only reads log files |

### Shared core (every job needs it)

| What | Where | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Start-up: log timestamps, `.env`, clients, gateway watchdog, `loginWithRetry` | `bot.js` | The Discord shell. Each extracted job needs its own copy, cut down to the clients and settings it uses. |
| Anthropic client | `bot.js` § Clients | One instance, passed into every factory. |
| Toggles | `src/toggles.js` | Three switches: `discord`, `telegram`, `scam-blocker` (`data/toggles.json`). |
| Usage and cost tracking | `trackUsage`, `loadUsageStats`, `PRICE_*` in `src/kb-sync.js` § Usage tracking | Sits in the KB sync file, but every Claude call in every job uses it (intent, claude, kb-monitor, reports). Belongs in its own file. |
| Date helpers | `getWeekRange`, `getDayRange`, `getMonthLabel`, `getWeekLabel`, `ensureDir` in `src/utils.js` | Used by answering (announcement capture) and reports. |
| Discord helpers | `isStaff`, `isBotMentioned`, `stripBotMention`, `trackerKey` in `src/utils.js` | `isStaff` is used by every Discord job. |
| `splitMessage` | `src/utils.js` | Telegram answers and reports. |
| **The intent classifier** | `classifyMessageIntent` in `src/intent.js` | **Shared by three jobs.** Answering uses its "respond" intents, Discord scam blocking uses `scam-content` (layers 1–2 run inside it), Telegram moderation uses `scam-content` and `community-conduct`. |
| Intent logs | `logMessageIntent`, `logIntentClassification`, `logTelegramMessage`, `logTelegramIntent` in `src/intent.js` | Written during answering and routing, read only by reports. |

### 1. Answering

**Own files:** `src/claude.js` (system prompt, scam-safety message for worried users (layers 4–5), re-ranking, live prices, the Sonnet call, conversation state, `pruneStaleEntries`, `loadCoreFacts`), `src/rag.js`, `src/embedder.js`, `src/kb-sync.js` (docs and blog sync, apart from usage tracking), `src/blog-scraper.js`, `src/kb-monitor.js`, `src/knowledge-loader.js` (explanation embed only), `src/price-fetcher.js`. Layers 4–5 stay with answering: they only add a safety paragraph to a reply and never punish anyone.

**Inside `src/commands.js`:**

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| Staff-wait timer and batching | § Timed auto-answer: `cancelPendingBatch`, `fireAutoAnswer`, `scheduleAutoAnswer` |
| Q&A learning | § Q&A learning (`markIfQuestion`) and the "Q&A learning (general + support)" block in `handleMessageCreate` |
| Explanation embed | § Explanation embed (`sendExplanationEmbed`) and the "@Bot explain" block |
| Deleted questions | § Deleted questions (the first `messageDelete` listener) |
| Manual KB adds | The `!add-blog-text` and `!add-doc-text` blocks |
| Announcement and tweet capture | The "Knowledge-capture channels" block |
| Routing | In `handleMessageCreate`: self-resolution, community reply, channel gate, Scenarios 0–3 (all except their `scam-content` branches), staff-engaged handling, community-discussion context |

**Inside `telegram/telegram-adapter.js`:** `sanitizeForTelegram`, `makeTgTarget`, `existingMessages`, § Timed auto-answer (Scenario 3), and the group `message` handler (Scenarios 0, 0.5, 1, 3, staff-engaged, community step-in). The group handler also does logging and the watched-user hand-off, which belong to reports and job 3.

**Inside `src/intent.js`:** `RESPOND_INTENTS`, `ALL_INTENT_CATEGORIES`, `INTENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT`, `classifyMessageIntent` (shared, see above).

**State (`src/state.js`):** `STAFF_WAIT_MS`, `REPHRASE_WINDOW_MS`, `MAX_BOT_ANSWERS_BEFORE_TICKET`, `CONV_EXPIRY_MS`, `STAFF_ENGAGED_WINDOW_MS`, `POST_STAFF_WAIT_MS`, `POST_STAFF_CONTEXT_MS`, `COMMUNITY_DISC_WINDOW_MS`, `REFERRAL_CODES`, `coreFacts`, `referralCode`, `pendingQuestions`, `pendingMsgIndex`, `rephrasingTracker`, `recentQuestions`, `conversationState`, `botMsgIndex`, `ragSourcesMap`, `staffEngaged`, `recentCommunityDiscussion`.

**Commands:** `/sync`, `/blog`, `/add-correction`, `/toggle platform:discord|telegram`, `/usage-stats` (shared), `!add-blog-text`, `!add-doc-text`.
**Timers:** the hourly `pruneStaleEntries` cron in `bot.js`.
**Settings:** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `VOYAGE_API_KEY`, `EMBEDDING_PROVIDER`, `GENERAL_CHANNEL_ID`, `SUPPORT_CHANNEL_ID`, `BOT_ANSWER_CHANNEL_IDS`, `ANNOUNCEMENTS_CHANNEL_ID`, `TWEETS_CHANNEL_ID`, `STAFF_EXPLANATION_CHANNEL_ID`, `STAFF_ROLE_IDS`, `STAFF_WAIT_MINUTES`, `CHINESE_DISCORD_CHANNEL_ID` (never answered); for Telegram, `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`, `TELEGRAM_TOPIC_IDS`, `CHINESE_TELEGRAM_TOPIC_ID`.
**Data:** `knowledge-base/`, `channel-learning/`, `data/usage-stats.json`.
**Tests:** `test/knowledge.test.js`; the channel-gate, deleted-question and Q&A-learning tests in `test/message-handler.test.js`; `stripBotMention`, `splitMessage`, `looksResolved`, system-prompt and Telegram deleted-message tests in `test/utils-and-reports.test.js`; `test/evals/`.

### 3. Telegram moderation

What it is today: a **manual watchlist only**. Admins put a user in a mode (watch, mute, kick or ban) from the staff DM. A watched or muted user's harmful messages are deleted and the admins are alerted, and the mode is applied again when the user rejoins. There is no automatic scam detection for other Telegram users (see `docs/DECISIONS.md`, "Telegram has no proactive scam blocking"). None of the Discord scam code is used: no layers 1–3, tweet check, infraction store or escalating timeouts.

**All inside `telegram/telegram-adapter.js`:**

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| Moderation store | § Perma-ban store: `PERMA_BAN_PATH`, `isPermaBanned`, `addPermaBan`, `removePermaBan`, `bumpRejoin` |
| Alert recipients | § Alert-admin store: `_loadAlertAdmins`, `_saveAlertAdmins`, `_getNotifyAdmins` |
| Admin check | § Admin cache: `isAdmin` (shared with answering and the staff panel) |
| Watched users | `watchedUsers`, `HARMFUL_INTENTS`, `handleWatchedMessage`, and the hand-off to it in the group `message` handler |
| Admin commands | The "Moderation commands" block in `handlePrivateDM`: `/tgban`, `/tgkick`, `/tgmute`, `/tgunmute`, `/tgwatch`, `/tgunkick`, `/tgunwatch`, `/tgunban`, `/tglist`, `/tgalerts` |
| Rejoin and captcha | The `chat_member` handler: re-applies ban, kick, mute or watch on rejoin, and mutes again after a captcha bot lifts a mute |

**Inside `src/intent.js`:** `checkWatchedFUD`, plus `classifyMessageIntent` (called with no message, so it gets no reply or thread context).
**Settings:** `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID`, `TELEGRAM_TOPIC_IDS`.
**Data:** `data/tg-perma-ban.json`, `data/tg-alert-admins.json`, `data/tg-watch-log.jsonl`.
**Tests:** none yet.
**River-specific:** almost nothing (the FUD prompt says "crypto project").

### Coupling to undo when splitting

How the code behaves today, and what has to change when the jobs are separated.

1. **Discord scam layers 1–2 have no entry point of their own.** They run inside `classifyMessageIntent`, which only the answer routing calls. So they check:
   - messages in answer channels (Scenario 3);
   - messages that @mention or reply to the bot;
   - the Chinese channel.

   Scenario 0 replies are never classified. **This coverage is the owner's choice** (`docs/DECISIONS.md`, "Discord scam layers 1–2 check only where the bot answers"): the busiest channels are where scammers wait, and other channels have link sharing off. The standalone scam blocker therefore needs its own checking step for these same channels. Make the channel list a setting, so another server can choose its own. **Decided (owner, 2026-11-15): the scam blocker keeps every feature it has today, including the full classifier.**
   - When Discord answering is on, answering and the scam blocker share one classification per message, so it costs nothing extra.
   - When Discord answering is off, the scam blocker classifies those messages itself, with the full classifier, so scams and spam are still caught.
2. **Toggles are tied together.** Today there are three: `discord`, `telegram` and `scam-blocker`. Turning off `discord` replies also stops layers 1–2, because its check in `handleMessageCreate` returns before the scenarios. Turning off `telegram` replies also stops watched-user deletions and Telegram logging, because both come after its check in the group `message` handler. See "Toggles" below for the design that replaces this.
3. **Telegram moderation only covers answer topics.** Watched users are checked only in `TELEGRAM_TOPIC_IDS` topics, so log-only topics (Chinese) are not moderated. Rejoin enforcement (`chat_member`) covers the whole group.
4. **`takeScamAction` and everything around it are closures inside `registerMessageHandler`.** They use its `discordClient`, config, `scamTracker`, `tweetResults` and `EmbedBuilder`. They need their own factory, such as `createScamBlocker(discordClient, config, deps)`.
5. **One Telegram file, four jobs.** The group handler mixes logging (reports), the watched-user hand-off (job 3) and routing (answering). The DM handler mixes the staff panel (reports) and admin commands (job 3). The `chat_member` handler mixes join/leave stats (reports) and rejoin enforcement (job 3).
6. **One slash-command file for all jobs.** `COMMANDS` and `handleInteraction` serve every job. Each job should register its own commands.
7. **Reports depend on loggers that sit in the routing code.** Moving reports to another bot means also moving the log calls (and the staff flag they record).

### Toggles (owner's design, 2026-11-15, not built yet)

Each job gets its own on/off switch for each platform, independent of every other switch, so a job can be paused on one platform without touching anything else. The switches are meant to be shown on a dashboard later.

| Switch | Controls | Replaces |
|---|---|---|
| Answers: Discord | Discord answering (Scenarios 0–3) | `discord` |
| Answers: Telegram | Telegram answering | `telegram` |
| Scam blocker: Discord | All of job 2 (layers 1–3, tweets, new-member links, DM watch, `takeScamAction`) | `scam-blocker` |
| Scam blocker: Telegram | Job 3: watched users, rejoin enforcement (ban / kick / mute / watch on rejoin, re-mute after captcha), and later any automatic detection | — (none today) |
| Reports | Job 4: `/report`, `/member-stats` and the Telegram staff panel | — (none today) |

Rules for building it (owner decisions, 2026-11-15):
- Turning off answering must not stop scam checks in the same channels. With answering on, the two share one classification per message. With answering off, the scam blocker runs the full classifier itself on the messages answering would have classified (see coupling 1).
- "Scam blocker: Telegram" covers rejoin enforcement for now. Today rejoin bans and mutes run whatever the switches say. Revisit when Telegram moderation becomes its own module.
- Logging for reports (intent, ticket, collab and join/leave logs) runs whatever the switches say, so reports never lose data. The Reports switch only turns off making reports, not collecting their data.
- Keep the switches in one store (today `src/toggles.js` / `data/toggles.json`). `/toggle` shows them all, and a dashboard can read and write the same store.
- Move the old `discord` / `telegram` / `scam-blocker` values in `data/toggles.json` to the new names, so current settings survive the change.

### Target layout (planned, not done)

Feature folders, each with a Discord and a Telegram subfolder (owner's choice, 2026-11-15). One folder per feature means one switch per folder (see Toggles), and moving a feature to another server means copying its folder plus `shared/` and `config/`. Folder names are placeholders: the owner will pick names that say what each part does.

```
bot.js              start-up only: settings, wiring
shared/             toggles, classifier (classifyMessageIntent), message logs, usage tracking,
                    date / Discord helpers, state
platforms/
  discord           the one Discord connection: receives each message, runs the classifier once
                    if any enabled feature needs it, hands the message to each enabled feature;
                    gathers every feature's slash commands
  telegram          the one Telegram bot: same job
answers/
  shared/           claude, rag, embedder, kb-sync, blog-scraper, kb-monitor, prices
  discord/          routing (Scenarios 0–3), timed auto-answer, explanation embed, KB staff commands
  telegram/         group answering, batching, Telegram formatting
scam-blocker/
  discord/          layers 1–3, tweet check, new-member links, DM watch, takeScamAction, scam-tracker
  telegram/         moderation store, alert admins, watched users, /tg… commands, rejoin enforcement
reports/
  shared/           community report
  discord/          member stats
  telegram/         member stats, staff panel
config/             River-specific values (links, IDs, prompts, referral codes, token addresses)
```

Each feature defines its own slash and `!` commands; `platforms/` only collects them, which splits up `src/slash-commands.js`.

Suggested order: reports (it only reads logs), then Telegram moderation (cut out of one file), then Discord scam blocking (needs its own entry point, see coupling 1). What is left is answering. Run `npm test` after each step. The existing tests cover each job's behaviour.

## When you add…

| You add | Also update |
|---|---|
| A code file | A row in the CLAUDE.md file map; a file header comment and `// ─── Section ───` headers; a purpose comment above each definition. Then `npm run index`. |
| A bug fix or behaviour change | A test in `test/` that fails without the change (`npm test`). A real wrong answer or misclassification → a case in `test/evals/cases.json` (`npm run eval`). |
| A code folder | Add it to `CODE_ROOTS` in `scripts/build-index.js` (or it stays invisible to the index and checks), give it a README.md, and add it to the file map. |
| A setting | `.env.example`, your `.env`, `docs/REFERENCE.md` § Settings and the code that reads it — the drift check compares all four. Read it in `bot.js` and pass it in, not inside a module. |
| A slash command | Its definition in `COMMANDS` and a `cmd === '…'` branch in `src/slash-commands.js`, a row in `docs/REFERENCE.md` § Commands, and `_dev-notes/Bot commands.txt` if the owner asks. |
| A Telegram or `!` command | Its handler, and a row in `docs/REFERENCE.md` § Commands. |
| An event listener or cron job | A row in `docs/REFERENCE.md` § Events or § Scheduled jobs. |
| A doc | Link it from CLAUDE.md or a README; long docs get a generated section list automatically. |
| A deliberate choice | A row in `docs/DECISIONS.md` with its reason. |
